অর্জন নিশ্চিত করা। মূল দায়িত্ব ও কর্তব্যসমূহ: সকল এরিয়া ম্যানেজার/শাখা ব্যবস্থাপক ও কর্মীদের তত্ত্বাবধান, দিকনির্দেশনা ও কার্যসম্পাদন নিশ্চিত করা। মাসে কমপক্ষে ১৮টি শাখা পরিদর্শন করা এবং পূর্ব যাচাই বাছাই সাপেক্ষে সিলিং অনুযায়ী ঋণ অনুমোদন এবং ঋণ ঋণের প্রকল্প তদারকি করা। নির্ধারিত সিলিং এর আওতায় অগ্রসর ঋণ সরেজমিনে যাচাই করা। বার্ষিক কর্মপরিকল্পনা ও বাজেট প্রস্তুত করা এবং কর্তৃপক্ষের অনুমোদনক্রমে বাস্তবায়ন করা। বিল ভাউচার যাচাই, সুপারিশ এবং সিলিং অনুযায়ী অনুমোদন দেওয়া। ঋণ বিতরণ, আদায়, সঞ্চয় ও পোর্টফোলিও ব্যবস্থাপনা নিশ্চিত করা সদস্য ভর্তি, ঋণ বিতরণ, সঞ্চয় সংগ্রহ এবং ঋণ আদায় কার্যক্রম নিয়মিতভাবে তদারকি করা। এরিয়ার আর্থিক লেনদেনের হিসাব-নিকাশ সঠিকভাবে রক্ষণাবেক্ষণ করা ও দৈনিক হিসাব প্রতিবেদন প্রস্তুত ও তদারকি করা। ঋণ বিতরণের পূর্বে সদস্যদের ঋণ যাচাই, গ্যারান্টি যাচাই ও ঋণ আবেদন অনুমোদনের প্রক্রিয়া তদারকি করা। তহবিল ব্যবস্থাপনা, ব্যাংক লেনদেন, নগদ টাকা উত্তোলন ও জমা কার্যক্রম তদারকি করা। কর্মসূচির দূর্নীতি ও আর্থিক অনিয়ম রোধ করা। অধীনস্থ কর্মীদের উপযুক্ত দিক নির্দেশনা দিয়ে সংস্থার নীতি ও আদর্শ মোতাবেক গড়ে তোলা। শাখা পরিদর্শনকালে শাখার তহবিল ব্যবস্থাপনা নিশ্চিত করা এবং ব্যাংক হিসাবের তদারকি করা। উর্ধ্বতন অফিস ও অধস্তন অফিসের মধ্যে সমন্বয় সাধন করা। মনিটরিং ব্যবস্থার মাধ্যমে অথবা সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্মীর দূর্বল দিক চিহ্নিত করে যথাপোযুক্ত ব্যবস্থা নেওয়া। গ্রাহক উন্নয়ন, ঝুঁকি ব্যবস্থাপনা ও ঋণ শৃঙ্খলা বজায় রাখা। ঋণ খেলাপি সদস্যদের বিষয়ে যথাযথ পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ এবং ঋণ আদায়ে কার্যকর ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ এবং তদারকি করা। এরিয়া/শাখা ব্যবস্থাপক/ফিল্ড সুপারভাইজার ও মাঠকর্মীদের কার্যক্রম পর্যবেক্ষণ ও কার্যসম্পাদন মূল্যায়ন (Performance Appraisal) এবং তাদের সক্ষমতা উন্নয়নে সহায়তা করা। মাসিক/ত্রৈমাসিক/বার্ষিক রিপোর্ট প্রস্তুত করে প্রধান কার্যালয়ে প্রেরণ করা। যাবতীয় নথিপত্র, রেজিস্টার ও দলিলসমূহ যথাযথভাবে সংরক্ষণে তদারকি করা। জোন/এরিয়া পর্যায়ে প্রশিক্ষণ, সচেতনতা সভা ও সদস্যদের উন্নয়নমূলক কার্যক্রম আয়োজন করা। স্থানীয় প্রশাসন, জনপ্রতিনিধি ও কমিউনিটির সঙ্গে সৌহার্দ্যপূর্ণ সম্পর্ক বজায় রাখা। শাখা পরিদর্শনকালে শাখার হিসাব নিকাশ ও আর্থিক যাবতীয় দিক যাচাই করা। সকল পর্যায়ে সদস্যদের সঞ্চয়, ঋণ ও অন্যান্য আর্থিক লেনদেনের বিষয়ে স্বচ্ছতা ও জবাবদিহিতা নিশ্চিত ও তদারকি করা। মাঠ পর্যায়ের সকল কার্যক্রমে তদারকি করা এবং নিয়মিত পর্যবেক্ষণ ও দিকনির্দেশনা প্রদান করা। সংস্থার সম্পদ ও সরঞ্জামের যথাযথ ব্যবহার নিশ্চিত ও তদারকি করা। সংস্থার নীতিমালা, নির্দেশিকা ও আচরণবিধি অনুসরণ করে সকল কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করা। ঊর্ধ্বতন কর্তৃপক্ষের নির্দেশনা অনুযায়ী অতিরিক্ত দায়িত্ব ও বিশেষ কার্যক্রম সম্পন্ন job_description: Job Context Eco-Social Development Organization (ESDO) started its journey in 1988 with a noble vision to stand in solidarity with the poor and marginalized. Being a people` centered organization, ESDO envisioned for a society which will be free from inequality and injustice, a society where no child will cry from hunger and no life will be ruined by poverty. Near about three decades of relentless efforts to make this happen, ESDO has embraced new grounds and opened up new horizons to help the disadvantaged and vulnerable people to bring meaningful and lasting changes in their lives. During this long span, ESDO has adapted with the changing situation and provided the most time-bound services especially for the poor and disadvantaged. A community focused and people centered approach has been adapted by ESDO while consideration was given to the national policy and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) as its guiding principle. ESDO is one of the most dynamic organizations expanding its development interventions across 422 upazilas under 56 districts of Bangladesh covering over 10 million poor and vulnerable people. ESDO is going to implement a UNICEF-supported project titled "Provide quality, inclusive skills development and Myanmar Curriculum STEM education for adolescent learners aged 15-18, and portable skills training for education volunteers in Cox`s Bazar" in Rohingya camps of Ukhia, Cox`s Bazar. The project aims to improve access to quality foundational literacy numeracy (FLN), trade skills, employability skills, leadership skills, entrepreneurship training, STEM Education and portable skills opportunities for Rohingya adolescents and youth through Multi-Purpose Centers (MPCs), Science and IT Labs, and SKILFO-based portable skills interventions. The Finance Associate is the operational backbone of the project`s finance function and first point of financial verification. The position is responsible for the day-to-day accounting, transaction processing, budget tracking, cash and bank management, financial documentation, and preparation of the financial reports and instruments that keep the project`s cash flow compliant with UNICEF`s Harmonized Approach to Cash Transfers (HACT) and audit-ready at all times. The position ensures that every financial transaction is recorded accurately, coded correctly against the approved budget, supported by complete documentation, and processed within the timelines that Direct Cash Transfer (DCT) cycles demand. The Finance Associate will work under the direct supervision of the Admin and Finance Manager and coordinate closely with the Procurement Associate, HR and Admin Associate, and programme colleagues to keep the project`s financial engine running smoothly. Reporting to: Direct reporting to Admin & Finance Manager Job Responsibilities 1. Financial Management, Accounting, and Transaction Processing Maintain project accounts, books of records, ledgers, and supporting documents in line with ESDO`s accounting policies, IPSAS standards, HACT policies and donor’s other requirements. Prepare payment vouchers, journal vouchers, cash vouchers, and bank vouchers with correct budget coding and complete supporting documentation. Verify bills, invoices, and supporting documents for accuracy, completeness, and compliance before payment processing. Record all financial transactions in the accounting system on time and with accurate output and activity-line coding. Maintain cash books, bank books, and all financial registers as per policy. 2. Budget Tracking, DCT Preparation, and Financial Reporting Track monthly expenditure against approved budget lines and flag under- or over-spend to the Admin and Finance Manager so that Direct Cash Transfer (DCT) funds are fully utilized within the quarter. Support in preparing inputs for DCT requests so that requests can be cleared and submitted to UNICEF at least fifteen days before the start of each quarter. Support in preparing liquidation documentation, FACE forms, and expenditure statements so that quarterly liquidation is completed and submitted within fifteen days of quarter end, in strict compliance with HACT timelines. Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports, budget variance analyses, and inputs to donor financial reports. Support budget forecasting and cash flow planning under the direction of the Admin and Finance Manager. 3. Cash and Bank Management Monitor project cash balances and banking transactions on a daily basis and prepare bank reconciliation statements on a regular basis. Maintain accurate records of cash advances, adjustments, settlements, and outstanding balances. Ensure secure handling of cheques, cash, and financial instruments in accordance with internal control procedures. Support cash flow monitoring, fund management, disbursement to prevent delays in payments to volunteers, vendors, and landowners. 4. Compliance, Statutory Obligations, and Documentation Ensure compliance with UNICEF financial guidelines, PCA requirements, HACT rules, and ESDO`s financial policies in every transaction process. Ensure statutory deductions (VAT, tax, and other levies) are calculated, withheld, and deposited to the relevant authorities on time, and that returns are filed in accordance with Government of Bangladesh requirements. Maintain complete, well-indexed, and secure financial documentation and filing systems (physical and electronic) for audit, spot check and donor review. Support the Admin and Finance Manager in responding to audit observations and implementing recommendations. 5. Audit Support, Internal Controls, and Risk Awareness Support internal audits, UNICEF financial spot checks, programmatic spot checks, HACT assurance activities, and any external or donor audits by providing accurate documentation, reconciliations, and explanations. Follow internal control procedures diligently, including segregation of duties, authorization thresholds, and dual-signature requirements. Stay alert to fraud risk indicators and unusual transactions, and escalate any concerns immediately to the Admin and Finance Manager. Contribute to the project`s risk register by flagging emerging financial or operational risks observed in day-to-day work. 6. Cross-Functional Financial Support Coordinate with the Procurement Associate, the other Finance Associate on payment processing, vendor documentation, and reconciliation of procurement transactions. Coordinate with the HR and Admin Associate on payroll processing, staff advances, volunteer incentive disbursements, and benefits payments. Support inventory and logistics records, verification, asset registration, and end-of-project asset transfer from the financial recording perspective. Provide timely financial information to programme colleagues so that decisions on activity implementation are informed by accurate expenditure data. Assist in administrative and operational financial matters as required. 7. Safeguarding, Accountability, and Ethical Practice Uphold the highest standards of Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Child Safeguarding (CSG), Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), and anti-fraud behavior in every financial transaction processed. Maintain strict confidentiality of financial, personnel, and community feedback information. Ensure that financial dealings with vendors, service providers, volunteers, and community members reflect integrity, transparency, and dignity. 8. job_description: Job Context Eco-Social Development Organization (ESDO) started its journey in 1988 with a noble vision to stand in solidarity with the poor and marginalized. Near about three decades of relentless efforts to make this happen, ESDO has embraced new grounds and opened up new horizons to help the disadvantaged and vulnerable people to bring meaningful and lasting changes in their lives. ESDO is one of the most dynamic organizations expanding its development interventions across 422 upazilas under 56 districts of Bangladesh covering over 10 million poor and vulnerable people. ESDO is going to implement a UNICEF-supported project titled "Provide quality, inclusive skills development and Myanmar Curriculum STEM education for adolescent learners aged 15-18, and portable skills training for education volunteers in Cox`s Bazar" in Rohingya camps of Ukhia, Cox`s Bazar. The project aims to improve access to quality foundational literacy numeracy (FLN), trade skills, employability skills, leadership skills, entrepreneurship training, STEM Education and portable skills opportunities for Rohingya adolescents and youth through Multi-Purpose Centers (MPCs), Science and IT Labs, and SKILFO-based portable skills interventions. The Warehouse Associate is responsible for the reliable, disciplined, and audit-defensible management of every physical resource that reaches learners under this project, including learning and teaching materials, tools and consumables materials, science and IT laboratory equipment, EdTech devices for instructors, safeguarding and awareness-raising materials, and general office and facility supplies. The position ensures that goods received against approved procurement are properly inspected, recorded, and stored; dispatched on time to the right multi-purpose centres and laboratories; supported by end-user monitoring evidence; and accounted for from the moment they enter the warehouse to the moment they are transferred at project closure. In a project of this scale, spread across multiple camps and facilities, the discipline of the warehouse function directly determines whether teaching happens on schedule and whether donor funds can be liquidated cleanly. The position will support efficient warehouse operations and timely availability of materials required for project implementation. Reporting to: Direct Reporting to Admin and Finance Manager Job Responsibilities 1. Warehouse Operations, Inventory Management, and Stock Control Maintain accurate warehouse records, stock registers, and inventory databases across every supply category for the project, including learning materials, trade course tools and consumables, laboratory equipment, EdTech devices, and office supplies. Receive, inspect, and record incoming goods against Goods Receipt Notes (GRN), verifying quantity, quality, specification, and condition before acceptance, and reporting any shortage, damage, or non-conformity to the Admin and Finance Manager immediately. Ensure proper storage, labelling, batching, and arrangement of materials so that stock is easily located, protected from damage, and organized for FIFI/LIFO issuance where applicable. Monitor stock levels against minimum thresholds and initiate timely replenishment requests through the Admin and Finance Manager to prevent stock-outs that would disrupt teaching or laboratory operations. Conduct periodic physical inventory counts and stock verification exercises, reconcile results with the inventory system, and document any variances with clear explanation. 2. Supply Dispatch, Last-Mile Coordination, and End-User Monitoring Prepare and issue stock issue vouchers, delivery notes, and dispatch documentation for every movement of goods leaving the warehouse. Coordinate with the Field Officer and Field Assistants on the sequencing, packing, transportation, and last-mile delivery of supplies to the multi-purpose centres, laboratories, and any other project locations. Ensure end-user monitoring documentation is captured for supplies dispatched, including receipt acknowledgements from field colleagues, photographic evidence where required, and follow-up on usage and condition of materials in the field. Support quarterly Post-Delivery Monitoring (PDM) and End-User Monitoring processes as agreed with UNICEF, and ensure evidence is filed and available for spot checks, audits, and monitoring visits. 3. Asset Management and End-of-Project Transfer Ensure every asset procured under the project is registered, tagged with a unique asset code, and entered into the asset register with complete documentation of specification, cost, source of funding, and assigned custodian. Maintain accurate asset movement records so that the location and condition of every asset can be traced at any time. Support periodic asset verification, physical checks, and reconciliation with the Finance Associate on asset value and depreciation records. Coordinate with the Admin and Finance Manager and the Skills Development Technical Lead on the planned transfer, disposal, or handover of assets at the end of the project, in line with donor requirements. Report damaged, lost, obsolete, or missing assets promptly and follow the required incident and write-off procedures. 4. Warehouse Safety, Storage Standards, and Environmental Safeguards Ensure the warehouse is kept clean, secure, well-ventilated, and organized to protect goods, staff, and visitors from damage or harm. Ensure appropriate segregation and safe storage of any potentially hazardous or sensitive materials associated with the trade courses (for example soap and hygiene product ingredients, solar and electrical components) and any laboratory consumables, in line with the project`s Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) Action Plan. Ensure fire safety equipment, first aid kits, and emergency exits are in place, accessible, and regularly checked, and that warehouse staff and guards understand emergency response procedures. Ensure environmentally responsible warehouse practices including regular pest control and fumigation practice, waste segregation, minimization of single-use plastics, and safe disposal of packaging and expired stock. E. Documentation, Reporting, Audit Support and Leadership Maintain warehouse files, inventory records, dispatch documentation, and asset records in a manner that supports quick retrieval for internal reviews, audits, HACT spot checks, donor monitoring visits, and end-of-project reporting. Prepare and submit monthly stock reports and periodic asset reports to the Admin and Finance Manager, in line with the reporting requirement. Ensure warehouse and asset records reconcile with procurement records held by the Procurement Associate and financial records held by the Finance Associate on a monthly basis. Support internal audits, UNICEF financial and programmatic spot checks, and any external or donor audits by providing accurate documentation, physical verification support, and explanations. Directly supervise the Warehouse Security Guards, setting clear expectations, work rotas, standards of conduct, and shift arrangements to ensure round-the-clock security of the warehouse F. Safeguarding and Accountability Uphold the highest standards of Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Child Safeguarding (CSG), Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), and anti-fraud behaviour in every warehouse transaction and interaction. Ensure warehouse operations reflect transparency and accountability, with no material leaving the warehouse without proper authorization and documentation and are utilized appropriately in field. Escalate any suspicion of theft, fraud, misuse, or safeguarding concern to the Admin and Finance Manager immediately. G. Assist the Supply and Logistic Officer in operational and warehouse management activities. Perform any other duties assigned by the Supply and Logistic Officer, Admin & Finance Manager, or Project Manager.

job_description: CIPLC is looking for a qualified and hands-on  Executive – Health & Safety  to support HSE implementation across assigned EPC project sites. The role will be responsible for implementing the project HSE plan, conducting hazard identification and risk assessments, managing permit-to-work requirements, conducting safety inspections and toolbox talks, delivering HSE inductions and training, monitoring subcontractor compliance, investigating incidents and near-misses, and maintaining HSE records and reports. The position will also support emergency response, first aid, fire safety and other site safety requirements in coordination with project teams and relevant stakeholders. HSE Plan & Risk Management: Implement the project HSE plan, safety procedures and site rules at assigned project sites. Conduct hazard identification, risk assessments and Job Safety Analyses (JSA) for site activities. Ensure identified risk controls are implemented and maintained. Support the Assistant Manager – QA & Planning in monitoring overall site HSE compliance. Permit-to-work & Site Safety: Manage the Permit-to-Work system for work at height, hot work, lifting, excavation and electrical works including LOTO. Conduct daily safety inspections and toolbox talks. Ensure proper use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Monitor site activities and stop unsafe work when required. Monitor housekeeping, waste management, dust and noise control at site. Training & Emergency Preparedness: Deliver HSE induction for new workers, subcontractors and visitors. Organize safety training programs and emergency drills. Ensure first aid, fire safety and emergency response arrangements are available at site. Promote safety awareness among workers and project teams. Equipment & Worksite Inspection: Inspect lifting equipment, scaffolding, ladders, tools and fire extinguishers. Inspect temporary electrical installations and monitor electrical safety requirements. Monitor compliance with work-at-height, lifting and other high-risk activity requirements. Incident Investigation & Corrective Actions: Investigate incidents and near-misses and identify root causes. Follow up on corrective and preventive actions. Report HSE violations and monitor resolution. Maintain appropriate incident and corrective-action records. HSE Reporting & Documentation: Maintain HSE registers, man-hour and incident statistics. Maintain inspection reports and training records. Prepare weekly and monthly HSE reports for the Assistant Manager – QA & Planning and the client. Maintain accurate HSE documentation and statistics.

job_description: About the Organization Shakti Foundation for Disadvantaged Women (Shakti Foundation) is a national development organization and microfinance institution working across Bangladesh since 1992. The organization is committed to the socio-economic empowerment of disadvantaged women through social and financial inclusion. Beginning with a pilot urban microfinance program for slum-dwelling women in Dhaka, Shakti Foundation has strategically expanded its service network into rural areas and now serves more than 6 lac members through a nationwide network of 648 branches across 57 districts. Alongside microfinance, its programming spans health, climate change, financial inclusion and women’s empowerment, supported by an extensive field presence and community-based delivery platforms. Shakti is registered with the NGO Affairs Bureau of Bangladesh under the Foreign Donations (Voluntary Activities) Regulation Rules and with the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms under the Societies Registration Act 1860. It is also licensed by the Microcredit Regulatory Authority (MRA) to operate its microfinance program. Bangladesh faces escalating climate risks, including extreme heat, flooding, cyclones, salinity intrusion, water stress, ecosystem degradation and climate-sensitive health threats. These risks affect low-income women and other vulnerable populations disproportionately and can disrupt Shakti Foundation’s operations, assets, workforce, clients and service delivery. At the same time, Shakti Foundation’s reach creates opportunities to integrate climate resilience, environmental responsibility and low-carbon practices across programs and institutional systems. Under the Inclusive Climate Finance for Vulnerable Communities in Asia Pacific (ICCAP) program, Shakti Foundation intends to engage a qualified consultant or consulting firm to develop an organization-wide Climate Strategy and a practical Monitoring & Reporting Framework. The assignment will translate climate commitments into prioritized, costed and measurable actions, with clear governance, indicators, data tools, accountability and reporting arrangements. Project Context The Inclusive Climate Finance for Vulnerable Communities in the Asia Pacific (ICCAP) is a five-year regional project implemented by a consortium of three partners: Appui au Développement Autonome (ADA), the Asia Pacific Rural and Agricultural Credit Association (APRACA), and the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI). The project aims to improve and scale up access to both public and private climate finance flows through Financial Service Providers (FSPs) to vulnerable communities across the Asia-Pacific region, including Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, Fiji, Lao PDR, and Nepal. The project is financed by the International Climate Initiative (IKI) as part of the German Government’s international climate finance commitment. In Bangladesh, ADA is providing technical assistance to partner FSPs, including Shakti Foundation, to strengthen their capacity to integrate climate considerations into financial products, institutional strategies, operations, and monitoring systems. Under Work Package 2, Activity 1.2 of the ICCAP Technical Assistance Grant, Shakti Foundation will develop and implement a Board-approved Integrated Climate Strategy covering climate finance and green internal operations; a Shakti climate finance taxonomy aligned with the Bangladesh Green Taxonomy; and a monitoring and reporting system that is embedded in Shakti's core ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) system and supported by a practical tracking tool for internal operations, with staff trained to use it. Objective The purpose of the consultancy is to provide Shakti Foundation with an evidence-based and implementable climate strategy, together with a monitoring and reporting system that enables the organization to plan, track, learn from and communicate its climate-related performance and results. Specifically, the consultancy will: Define a climate vision, strategic objectives and a 5-year roadmap aligned with Shakti’s institutional mission and its focus on women (Action 1.2.1). Develop an institutional climate finance taxonomy aligned with the Bangladesh Green Taxonomy and contextualized to Shakti Foundation’s target clients, priority sectors, financial products, and operational model (Action 1.2.2). Develop an internal Green Operations Strategy to strengthen Shakti Foundation’s environmental performance, with a focus on paper reduction, energy efficiency, waste management, and other relevant operational measures (Action 1.2.3). Facilitate stakeholder workshops, board presentation and formal approval of an Integrated Climate Strategy (Action 1.2.4). Establish a Climate Monitoring and Reporting Framework by defining standardized indicators for the climate portfolio covering climate finance and green internal operations, along with standardized reporting templates and practical data requirements (Action 1.2.5). Specify the data requirements for, and quality-assure, the integration of taxonomy and climate finance indicators into Shakti’s core ERP system by Shakti’s IT team (Action 1.2.6). Establish an Excel-based tracking system for internal green operations indicators to support regular data collection, monitoring, analysis, and reporting of Shakti Foundation’s environmental performance (Action 1.2.7). Strengthen institutional capacity by building the knowledge and skills of relevant Shakti Foundation staff to implement the Climate Strategy and M&R Framework, collect and manage climate-related data, track indicators and effectively use reporting tools and dashboards (Action 1.2.8). Expected Outputs Inception Report, including the detailed work plan and allocation of professional days. Board-approved Integrated Climate Strategy for Shakti, incorporating climate finance vision, objectives and strategic roadmap. Shakti Climate Finance Taxonomy aligned with the Bangladesh Green Taxonomy, with loan categorization codes, ERP tags, application guidance, product mapping, pilot results and an indicative portfolio estimate. Internal Green Operations Strategy with baseline assessment, targets, costed measures and green office guidelines. Stakeholder Consultation Reports and Board Presentation. Climate Monitoring and Reporting Framework, including indicator reference sheets and three core reporting templates. ERP Data Requirements Specification, test scenarios and ERP Integration Review Note. Tested Excel Internal Operations Tracking Tool and User Guide. SOP Manual, Training Materials and Training-of-Trainers Completion Report with cascade plan. Final Assignment Report and Handover Package. Duration and Working Modality Duration:  6 months from contract signing Work Approach: Evidence-Based Assessment: Conduct comprehensive desk reviews, data-gap assessments, and climate risk/vulnerability analyses that merge credible secondary data with institutional and community-level experiences. Participatory Engagement & Co-Design: Facilitate key-informant interviews, field visits, and focused co-design sessions across all levels—from frontline staff and community stakeholders to program/support functions—to ensure deep institutional ownership of the strategy and monitoring frameworks. Iterative Development & Testing: Utilize a feedback-driven process to draft, validate, and practically pilot-test strategies, monitoring indicators, and tools before finalization. Capacity Building: Deliver targeted training and capacity-building initiatives to ensure the organization can seamlessly implement and sustain the new frameworks. Ethical & Inclusive Integration: Mainstream gender equality, social inclusion, safeguarding, "do-no-harm" principles, data protection, and ethical participation throughout all phases of the assignment. Alignment by design: outputs are developed against international climate finance conventions from the outset, so that they remain usable as Shakti's funding base widens, without substantial rework. Field Requirements: Field engagement at selected branches is required for the operations baseline, pilot testing and staff training. Coordination: Close coordination with Shakti Foundation Technical Working Group and ICCAP focal persons. A Technical Working Group (TWG) will be formed, comprising representatives from Shakti Foundation Climate Change Program, Microfinance Operations, Finance and Accounts, IT, Administration, Procurement, Human Resources and relevant operational units. Shakti will provide access to relevant institutional data, systems, staff and branch locations, subject to its confidentiality and data protection requirements. The Consultant/Firm is responsible for its own logistics, equipment, travel and workspace arrangements unless otherwise agreed.
